text: Just then. <break time="0.8s" /> Toto jumped out of Dorothys arms. <break time="0.8s" /> And hid under the bed. <break time="0.8s" /> While the girl tried to get him. <break time="0.8s" /> Aunt Em threw open the trap door. <break time="0.8s" /> Badly frightened. <break time="0.8s" /> She climbed down the ladder. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the small, dark hole. <break time="0.8s" /> At last Dorothy caught Toto. <break time="0.8s" /> And started to follow her aunt. <break time="0.8s" /> When she was halfway across the room. <break time="0.8s" /> There came a great shriek. <break time="0.8s" /> From the wind. <break time="0.8s" /> The house shook so hard. <break time="0.8s" /> That she lost her footing. <break time="0.8s" /> And sat down suddenly on the floor. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a strange thing happened. <break time="0.8s" /> The house whirled around. <break time="0.8s" /> Two or three times. <break time="0.8s" /> And rose slowly through the air. <break time="0.8s" /> The north wind and the south wind. <break time="0.8s" /> Met at the very place. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the house stood. <break time="0.8s" /> That place became. <break time="0.8s" /> The exact center of the cyclone. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the air is usually still. <break time="0.8s" /> But the strong wind on every side. <break time="0.8s" /> Pushed the house higher and higher. <break time="0.8s" /> At the very top of the cyclone. <break time="0.8s" /> It was carried. <break time="0.8s" /> Miles and miles away. <break time="0.8s" /> As easily as a feather.
